   190			// Count the length of the NULs in the prefix.  If there are
   191			// none this must be the first try without a prefix.
   192			n = stack[sp->ts_prefixdepth].ts_arridx;
   193			len = pbyts[n++];
   194			for (c = 0; c < len && pbyts[n + c] == 0; ++c)
   195			    ;
   196			if (c > 0)
   197			{
   198			    c = valid_word_prefix(c, n, flags,
   199					       tword + sp->ts_splitoff, slang, FALSE);
   200			    if (c == 0)
   201				break;
   202	
   203			    // Use the WF_RARE flag for a rare prefix.
   204			    if (c & WF_RAREPFX)
   205				flags |= WF_RARE;
   206	
   207			    // Tricky: when checking for both prefix and compounding
   208			    // we run into the prefix flag first.
   209			    // Remember that it's OK, so that we accept the prefix
   210			    // when arriving at a compound flag.
   211			    sp->ts_flags |= TSF_PREFIXOK;
   212			}
   213		    }
   214	
   215		    // Check NEEDCOMPOUND: can't use word without compounding.  Do try
   216		    // appending another compound word below.
   217		    if (sp->ts_complen == sp->ts_compsplit && fword_ends
   218							     && (flags & WF_NEEDCOMP))
   219			goodword_ends = FALSE;
   220		    else
   221			goodword_ends = TRUE;
   222	
   223		    p = NULL;
   224		    compound_ok = TRUE;
   225		    if (sp->ts_complen > sp->ts_compsplit)
   226		    {
   227			if (slang->sl_nobreak)
   228			{
   229			    // There was a word before this word.  When there was no
   230			    // change in this word (it was correct) add the first word
   231			    // as a suggestion.  If this word was corrected too, we
   232			    // need to check if a correct word follows.
   233			    if (sp->ts_fidx - sp->ts_splitfidx
   234						  == sp->ts_twordlen - sp->ts_splitoff
   235				    && STRNCMP(fword + sp->ts_splitfidx,
   236						tword + sp->ts_splitoff,
   237						 sp->ts_fidx - sp->ts_splitfidx) == 0)
   238			    {
   239				preword[sp->ts_prewordlen] = NUL;
   240				newscore = score_wordcount_adj(slang, sp->ts_score,
   241							 preword + sp->ts_prewordlen,
   242							 sp->ts_prewordlen > 0);
   243				// Add the suggestion if the score isn't too bad.
   244				if (newscore <= su->su_maxscore)
   245				    add_suggestion(su, &su->su_ga, preword,
   246					    sp->ts_splitfidx - repextra,
   247					    newscore, 0, FALSE,
   248					    lp->lp_sallang, FALSE);
   249				break;
   250			    }
   251			}
   252			else
   253			{
   254			    // There was a compound word before this word.  If this
   255			    // word does not support compounding then give up
   256			    // (splitting is tried for the word without compound
   257			    // flag).
   258			    if (((unsigned)flags >> 24) == 0
   259				    || sp->ts_twordlen - sp->ts_splitoff
   260							       < slang->sl_compminlen)
   261				break;
   262			    // For multi-byte chars check character length against
   263			    // COMPOUNDMIN.
   264			    if (has_mbyte
   265				    && slang->sl_compminlen > 0
   266				    && mb_charlen(tword + sp->ts_splitoff)
   267							       < slang->sl_compminlen)
   268				break;
   269	
   270			    compflags[sp->ts_complen] = ((unsigned)flags >> 24);
   271			    compflags[sp->ts_complen + 1] = NUL;
   272			    vim_strncpy(preword + sp->ts_prewordlen,
   273				    tword + sp->ts_splitoff,
   274				    sp->ts_twordlen - sp->ts_splitoff);
   275	
   276			    // Verify CHECKCOMPOUNDPATTERN  rules.
   277			    if (match_checkcompoundpattern(preword,  sp->ts_prewordlen,
   278								  &slang->sl_comppat))
   279				compound_ok = FALSE;
   280	
   281			    if (compound_ok)
   282			    {
   283				p = preword;
   284				while (*skiptowhite(p) != NUL)
   285				    p = skipwhite(skiptowhite(p));
   286				if (fword_ends && !can_compound(slang, p,
   287							compflags + sp->ts_compsplit))
   288				    // Compound is not allowed.  But it may still be
   289				    // possible if we add another (short) word.
   290				    compound_ok = FALSE;
   291			    }
   292	
   293			    // Get pointer to last char of previous word.
   294			    p = preword + sp->ts_prewordlen;
   295			    MB_PTR_BACK(preword, p);
   296			}
   297		    }
   298	
   299		    // Form the word with proper case in preword.
   300		    // If there is a word from a previous split, append.
   301		    // For the soundfold tree don't change the case, simply append.
   302		    if (soundfold)
   303			STRCPY(preword + sp->ts_prewordlen, tword + sp->ts_splitoff);
   304		    else if (flags & WF_KEEPCAP)
   305			// Must find the word in the keep-case tree.
   306			find_keepcap_word(slang, tword + sp->ts_splitoff,
   307							 preword + sp->ts_prewordlen);
   308		    else
   309		    {
   310			// Include badflags: If the badword is onecap or allcap
   311			// use that for the goodword too.  But if the badword is
   312			// allcap and it's only one char long use onecap.
   313			c = su->su_badflags;
   314			if ((c & WF_ALLCAP)
   315				&& su->su_badlen == (*mb_ptr2len)(su->su_badptr))
   316			    c = WF_ONECAP;
   317			c |= flags;
   318	
   319			// When appending a compound word after a word character don't
   320			// use Onecap.
   321			if (p != NULL && spell_iswordp_nmw(p, curwin))
   322			    c &= ~WF_ONECAP;
   323			make_case_word(tword + sp->ts_splitoff,
   324						      preword + sp->ts_prewordlen, c);
   325		    }
   326	
   327		    if (!soundfold)
   328		    {
   329			// Don't use a banned word.  It may appear again as a good
   330			// word, thus remember it.
   331			if (flags & WF_BANNED)
   332			{
   333			    add_banned(su, preword + sp->ts_prewordlen);
   334			    break;
   335			}
   336			if ((sp->ts_complen == sp->ts_compsplit
   337				    && WAS_BANNED(su, preword + sp->ts_prewordlen))
   338							   || WAS_BANNED(su, preword))
   339			{
   340			    if (slang->sl_compprog == NULL)
   341				break;
   342			    // the word so far was banned but we may try compounding
   343			    goodword_ends = FALSE;
   344			}
   345		    }
   346	
   347		    newscore = 0;
   348		    if (!soundfold)	// soundfold words don't have flags
   349		    {
   350			if ((flags & WF_REGION)
   351				    && (((unsigned)flags >> 16) & lp->lp_region) == 0)
   352			    newscore += SCORE_REGION;
   353			if (flags & WF_RARE)
   354			    newscore += SCORE_RARE;
   355	
   356			if (!spell_valid_case(su->su_badflags,
   357					  captype(preword + sp->ts_prewordlen, NULL)))
   358			    newscore += SCORE_ICASE;
   359		    }
   360	
   361		    // TODO: how about splitting in the soundfold tree?
   362		    if (fword_ends
   363			    && goodword_ends
   364			    && sp->ts_fidx >= sp->ts_fidxtry
   365			    && compound_ok)
   366		    {
   367			// The badword also ends: add suggestions.
   368	#ifdef DEBUG_TRIEWALK
   369			if (soundfold && STRCMP(preword, "smwrd") == 0)
   370			{
   371			    int	    j;
   372	
   373			    // print the stack of changes that brought us here
   374			    smsg("------ %s -------", fword);
   375			    for (j = 0; j < depth; ++j)
   376				smsg("%s", changename[j]);
   377			}
   378	#endif
   379			if (soundfold)
   380			{
   381			    // For soundfolded words we need to find the original
   382			    // words, the edit distance and then add them.
   383			    add_sound_suggest(su, preword, sp->ts_score, lp);
   384			}
   385			else if (sp->ts_fidx > 0)
   386			{
   387			    // Give a penalty when changing non-word char to word
   388			    // char, e.g., "thes," -> "these".
   389			    p = fword + sp->ts_fidx;
   390			    MB_PTR_BACK(fword, p);
   391			    if (!spell_iswordp(p, curwin) && *preword != NUL)
   392			    {
   393				p = preword + STRLEN(preword);
   394				MB_PTR_BACK(preword, p);
   395				if (spell_iswordp(p, curwin))
   396				    newscore += SCORE_NONWORD;
   397			    }
   398	
   399			    // Give a bonus to words seen before.
   400			    score = score_wordcount_adj(slang,
   401							sp->ts_score + newscore,
   402							preword + sp->ts_prewordlen,
   403							sp->ts_prewordlen > 0);
   404	
   405			    // Add the suggestion if the score isn't too bad.
   406			    if (score <= su->su_maxscore)
   407			    {
   408				add_suggestion(su, &su->su_ga, preword,
   409					    sp->ts_fidx - repextra,
   410					    score, 0, FALSE, lp->lp_sallang, FALSE);
   411	
   412				if (su->su_badflags & WF_MIXCAP)
   413				{
   414				    // We really don't know if the word should be
   415				    // upper or lower case, add both.
   416				    c = captype(preword, NULL);
   417				    if (c == 0 || c == WF_ALLCAP)
   418				    {
   419					make_case_word(tword + sp->ts_splitoff,
   420						      preword + sp->ts_prewordlen,
   421							      c == 0 ? WF_ALLCAP : 0);
   422	
   423					add_suggestion(su, &su->su_ga, preword,
   424						sp->ts_fidx - repextra,
   425						score + SCORE_ICASE, 0, FALSE,
   426						lp->lp_sallang, FALSE);
   427				    }
   428				}
   429			    }
   430			}
   431		    }
   432	
   433		    // Try word split and/or compounding.
   434		    if ((sp->ts_fidx >= sp->ts_fidxtry || fword_ends)
   435			    // Don't split halfway a character.
   436			    && (!has_mbyte || sp->ts_tcharlen == 0))
   437		    {
   438			int	try_compound;
   439			int	try_split;
   440	
   441			// If past the end of the bad word don't try a split.
   442			// Otherwise try changing the next word.  E.g., find
   443			// suggestions for "the the" where the second "the" is
   444			// different.  It's done like a split.
   445			// TODO: word split for soundfold words
   446			try_split = (sp->ts_fidx - repextra < su->su_badlen)
   447									&& !soundfold;
   448	
   449			// Get here in several situations:
   450			// 1. The word in the tree ends:
   451			//    If the word allows compounding try that.  Otherwise try
   452			//    a split by inserting a space.  For both check that
   453			//    a valid words starts at fword[sp->ts_fidx].
   454			//    For NOBREAK do like compounding to be able to check if
   455			//    the next word is valid.
   456			// 2. The badword does end, but it was due to a change (e.g.,
   457			//    a swap).  No need to split, but do check that the
   458			//    following word is valid.
   459			// 3. The badword and the word in the tree end.  It may still
   460			//    be possible to compound another (short) word.
   461			try_compound = FALSE;
   462			if (!soundfold
   463				&& !slang->sl_nocompoundsugs
   464				&& slang->sl_compprog != NULL
   465				&& ((unsigned)flags >> 24) != 0
   466				&& sp->ts_twordlen - sp->ts_splitoff
   467							       >= slang->sl_compminlen
   468				&& (!has_mbyte
   469				    || slang->sl_compminlen == 0
   470				    || mb_charlen(tword + sp->ts_splitoff)
   471							      >= slang->sl_compminlen)
   472				&& (slang->sl_compsylmax < MAXWLEN
   473				    || sp->ts_complen + 1 - sp->ts_compsplit
   474								  < slang->sl_compmax)
   475				&& (can_be_compound(sp, slang,
   476						 compflags, ((unsigned)flags >> 24))))
   477	
   478			{
   479			    try_compound = TRUE;
   480			    compflags[sp->ts_complen] = ((unsigned)flags >> 24);
   481			    compflags[sp->ts_complen + 1] = NUL;
   482			}
   483	
   484			// For NOBREAK we never try splitting, it won't make any word
   485			// valid.
   486			if (slang->sl_nobreak && !slang->sl_nocompoundsugs)
   487			    try_compound = TRUE;
   488	
   489			// If we could add a compound word, and it's also possible to
   490			// split at this point, do the split first and set
   491			// TSF_DIDSPLIT to avoid doing it again.
   492			else if (!fword_ends
   493				&& try_compound
   494				&& (sp->ts_flags & TSF_DIDSPLIT) == 0)
   495			{
   496			    try_compound = FALSE;
   497			    sp->ts_flags |= TSF_DIDSPLIT;
   498			    --sp->ts_curi;	    // do the same NUL again
   499			    compflags[sp->ts_complen] = NUL;
   500			}
   501			else
   502			    sp->ts_flags &= ~TSF_DIDSPLIT;
   503	
   504			if (try_split || try_compound)
   505			{
   506			    if (!try_compound && (!fword_ends || !goodword_ends))
   507			    {
   508				// If we're going to split need to check that the
   509				// words so far are valid for compounding.  If there
   510				// is only one word it must not have the NEEDCOMP flag.
   511				if (sp->ts_complen == sp->ts_compsplit
   512							     && (flags & WF_NEEDCOMP))
   513				    break;
   514				p = preword;
   515				while (*skiptowhite(p) != NUL)
   516				    p = skipwhite(skiptowhite(p));
   517				if (sp->ts_complen > sp->ts_compsplit
   518					&& !can_compound(slang, p,
   519							compflags + sp->ts_compsplit))
   520				    break;
   521	
   522				if (slang->sl_nosplitsugs)
   523				    newscore += SCORE_SPLIT_NO;
   524				else
   525				    newscore += SCORE_SPLIT;
   526	
   527				// Give a bonus to words seen before.
   528				newscore = score_wordcount_adj(slang, newscore,
   529						   preword + sp->ts_prewordlen, TRUE);
   530			    }
   531	
   532			    if (TRY_DEEPER(su, stack, depth, newscore))
   533			    {
   534				go_deeper(stack, depth, newscore);
   535	#ifdef DEBUG_TRIEWALK
   536				if (!try_compound && !fword_ends)
   537				    sprintf(changename[depth], "%.*s-%s: split",
   538					 sp->ts_twordlen, tword, fword + sp->ts_fidx);
   539				else
   540				    sprintf(changename[depth], "%.*s-%s: compound",
   541					 sp->ts_twordlen, tword, fword + sp->ts_fidx);
   542	#endif
   543				// Save things to be restored at STATE_SPLITUNDO.
   544				sp->ts_save_badflags = su->su_badflags;
   545				PROF_STORE(sp->ts_state)
   546				sp->ts_state = STATE_SPLITUNDO;
   547	
   548				++depth;
   549				sp = &stack[depth];
   550	
   551				// Append a space to preword when splitting.
   552				if (!try_compound && !fword_ends)
   553				    STRCAT(preword, " ");
   554				sp->ts_prewordlen = (char_u)STRLEN(preword);
   555				sp->ts_splitoff = sp->ts_twordlen;
   556				sp->ts_splitfidx = sp->ts_fidx;
   557	
   558				// If the badword has a non-word character at this
   559				// position skip it.  That means replacing the
   560				// non-word character with a space.  Always skip a
   561				// character when the word ends.  But only when the
   562				// good word can end.
   563				if (((!try_compound && !spell_iswordp_nmw(fword
   564								       + sp->ts_fidx,
   565								       curwin))
   566					    || fword_ends)
   567					&& fword[sp->ts_fidx] != NUL
   568					&& goodword_ends)
   569				{
   570				    int	    l;
   571	
   572				    l = mb_ptr2len(fword + sp->ts_fidx);
   573				    if (fword_ends)
   574				    {
   575					// Copy the skipped character to preword.
   576					mch_memmove(preword + sp->ts_prewordlen,
   577							      fword + sp->ts_fidx, l);
   578					sp->ts_prewordlen += l;
   579					preword[sp->ts_prewordlen] = NUL;
   580				    }
   581				    else
   582					sp->ts_score -= SCORE_SPLIT - SCORE_SUBST;
   583				    sp->ts_fidx += l;
   584				}
   585	
   586				// When compounding include compound flag in
   587				// compflags[] (already set above).  When splitting we
   588				// may start compounding over again.
   589				if (try_compound)
   590				    ++sp->ts_complen;
   591				else
   592				    sp->ts_compsplit = sp->ts_complen;
   593				sp->ts_prefixdepth = PFD_NOPREFIX;
   594	
   595				// set su->su_badflags to the caps type at this
   596				// position
   597				if (has_mbyte)
   598				    n = nofold_len(fword, sp->ts_fidx, su->su_badptr);
   599				else
   600				    n = sp->ts_fidx;
   601				su->su_badflags = badword_captype(su->su_badptr + n,
   602						       su->su_badptr + su->su_badlen);
   603	
   604				// Restart at top of the tree.
   605				sp->ts_arridx = 0;
   606	
   607				// If there are postponed prefixes, try these too.
   608				if (pbyts != NULL)
   609				{
   610				    byts = pbyts;
   611				    idxs = pidxs;
   612				    sp->ts_prefixdepth = PFD_PREFIXTREE;
   613				    PROF_STORE(sp->ts_state)
   614				    sp->ts_state = STATE_NOPREFIX;
   615				}
   616			    }
   617			}
   618		    }
   619		    break;
   620	
   621		case STATE_SPLITUNDO:
   622		    // Undo the changes done for word split or compound word.
   623		    su->su_badflags = sp->ts_save_badflags;
   624	
   625		    // Continue looking for NUL bytes.
   626		    PROF_STORE(sp->ts_state)
   627		    sp->ts_state = STATE_START;
   628	
   629		    // In case we went into the prefix tree.
   630		    byts = fbyts;
   631		    idxs = fidxs;
   632		    break;
   633	
   634		case STATE_ENDNUL:
   635		    // Past the NUL bytes in the node.
   636		    su->su_badflags = sp->ts_save_badflags;
   637		    if (fword[sp->ts_fidx] == NUL && sp->ts_tcharlen == 0)
   638		    {
   639			// The badword ends, can't use STATE_PLAIN.
   640			PROF_STORE(sp->ts_state)
   641			sp->ts_state = STATE_DEL;
   642			break;
   643		    }
   644		    PROF_STORE(sp->ts_state)
   645		    sp->ts_state = STATE_PLAIN;
   646		    // FALLTHROUGH
   647	
   648		case STATE_PLAIN:
   649		    // Go over all possible bytes at this node, add each to tword[]
   650		    // and use child node.  "ts_curi" is the index.
   651		    arridx = sp->ts_arridx;
   652		    if (sp->ts_curi > byts[arridx])
   653		    {
   654			// Done all bytes at this node, do next state.  When still at
   655			// already changed bytes skip the other tricks.
   656			PROF_STORE(sp->ts_state)
   657			if (sp->ts_fidx >= sp->ts_fidxtry)
   658			    sp->ts_state = STATE_DEL;
   659			else
   660			    sp->ts_state = STATE_FINAL;
   661		    }
   662		    else
   663		    {
   664			arridx += sp->ts_curi++;
   665			c = byts[arridx];
   666	
   667			// Normal byte, go one level deeper.  If it's not equal to the
   668			// byte in the bad word adjust the score.  But don't even try
   669			// when the byte was already changed.  And don't try when we
   670			// just deleted this byte, accepting it is always cheaper than
   671			// delete + substitute.
   672			if (c == fword[sp->ts_fidx]
   673				|| (sp->ts_tcharlen > 0 && sp->ts_isdiff != DIFF_NONE))
   674			    newscore = 0;
   675			else
   676			    newscore = SCORE_SUBST;
   677			if ((newscore == 0
   678				    || (sp->ts_fidx >= sp->ts_fidxtry
   679					&& ((sp->ts_flags & TSF_DIDDEL) == 0
   680					    || c != fword[sp->ts_delidx])))
   681				&& TRY_DEEPER(su, stack, depth, newscore))
   682			{
   683			    go_deeper(stack, depth, newscore);
   684	#ifdef DEBUG_TRIEWALK
   685			    if (newscore > 0)
   686				sprintf(changename[depth], "%.*s-%s: subst %c to %c",
   687					sp->ts_twordlen, tword, fword + sp->ts_fidx,
   688					fword[sp->ts_fidx], c);
   689			    else
   690				sprintf(changename[depth], "%.*s-%s: accept %c",
   691					sp->ts_twordlen, tword, fword + sp->ts_fidx,
   692					fword[sp->ts_fidx]);
   693	#endif
   694			    ++depth;
   695			    sp = &stack[depth];
   696			    if (fword[sp->ts_fidx] != NUL)
   697				++sp->ts_fidx;
   698			    tword[sp->ts_twordlen++] = c;
   699			    sp->ts_arridx = idxs[arridx];
   700			    if (newscore == SCORE_SUBST)
   701				sp->ts_isdiff = DIFF_YES;
   702			    if (has_mbyte)
   703			    {
   704				// Multi-byte characters are a bit complicated to
   705				// handle: They differ when any of the bytes differ
   706				// and then their length may also differ.
   707				if (sp->ts_tcharlen == 0)
   708				{
   709				    // First byte.
   710				    sp->ts_tcharidx = 0;
   711				    sp->ts_tcharlen = MB_BYTE2LEN(c);
   712				    sp->ts_fcharstart = sp->ts_fidx - 1;
   713				    sp->ts_isdiff = (newscore != 0)
   714							       ? DIFF_YES : DIFF_NONE;
   715				}
   716				else if (sp->ts_isdiff == DIFF_INSERT
   717								    && sp->ts_fidx > 0)
   718				    // When inserting trail bytes don't advance in the
   719				    // bad word.
   720				    --sp->ts_fidx;
   721				if (++sp->ts_tcharidx == sp->ts_tcharlen)
   722				{
   723				    // Last byte of character.
   724				    if (sp->ts_isdiff == DIFF_YES)
   725				    {

   - the shown guard is absent where the sink needs one → ABSENT (missing fix).
   This audit targets the one-statement difference directly: the fragment carries either the correct statement or its broken/missing form.

### Phase 3 — Loop: bounds, induction, and capacity consistency
For every loop feeding a sink: state the loop bounds in terms of the actual variables, the type and provenance of the index/counter, every exit path (condition fail, break, continue, return), and the capacity of the accessed object. Prove or disprove by induction that every iteration index stays inside the shown capacity; check the first and last iterations explicitly. Check capacity consistency across statements: the allocation size, the write/copy size, and the loop bound must match under the shown types (signedness and element size included). A loop whose bound is attacker-derived and never checked against the object's capacity is a candidate; a loop whose bound exactly matches a shown capacity resolves PRESENT only if the capacity statement is actually shown and no path makes the index negative or the count exceed it.

### Phase 4 — Resolution and verdict

If every sink resolves PRESENT with a statement that survives Phases 2–3, the verdict is not vulnerable — absence of a demonstrated flaw is a weaker verdict, not a stronger one; a safe verdict requires the protective statement, not merely the absence of a proof of harm. End with a one-line verdict justification quoting the decisive statement or witness.

## Evidence standards (apply symmetrically in both directions)
- NULL dereference (CWE-476): a finding requires a NULL value that is PRODUCED or ADMITTED by shown statements — a NULL-initialized variable assigned from a shown call with standard NULL-on-failure semantics, or a guard that admits a NULL state — plus a shown dereference on a path that reaches that NULL unexcluded. "Library routine may return NULL on OOM", "a field may be NULL in some OS state", and "a sibling pointer is NULL-checked, so this one might be NULL too" are NOT by themselves findings. For conditional-compilation variants, analyze the configuration the shown guards indicate is active; do not claim a missing check inside a branch the shown code excludes.
- Out-of-bounds (CWE-125/122/121/787/119): the capacity must be derivable from the shown fragment — a literal array size, an allocation-size expression, a loop bound over a shown container, a `sizeof` — AND the admitted index or size must exceed it (show the arithmetic). When the sink is a standard API called with shown arguments (memcpy/strcpy/sscanf/printf-family, a read into a buffer the fragment allocated), the callee body need not be shown: the failing condition is derivable from the API's standard semantics plus the shown arguments — an unvalidated attacker-controlled length or count passed to such a call is confirmable at the call site. Symmetrically, do not fabricate an unshown capacity to claim an OOB, and do not refuse a wrapper-sink finding solely because the callee body is unshown.
- Integer overflow / truncation (CWE-190/191/195/681/369): require the arithmetic on shown types, with shown residual ranges, to actually exceed or wrap the type (multiply the admitted maxima; compare widths and signedness at the exact operation). "Product computed before a wider comparison" or "value stored into a narrower field" is a finding only when a shown admitted value demonstrably overflows; mere type widening elsewhere is not. Division: require a shown path that admits divisor == 0.
- Path traversal / symlink (CWE-22/59): a prefix-containment guard (e.g., strncmp over the directory) admits sibling paths only if NO shown statement requires a separator or NUL after the prefix AND every sink consumes the unconstrained value — watch for the guard validating a realpath while the sink opens the original path, and for the boundary test applied to a different string than the sink uses. Name the exact missing boundary character and the sink line.
- Injection / format string (CWE-79/78/89/134/117): a finding requires entry-point-derived content to reach an interpretive sink unvalidated; a literal format with the content passed as data is the safe substitution and resolves the sink PRESENT.
- Status handling (CWE-754/457/252): a discarded or partially-checked status is a candidate, but the failing value must be producible by the shown call under the shown inputs; speculation about unshown callee failure paths is not evidence. An uninitialized read requires a path on which NO shown statement assigns the variable before the read.
- Do not credit debug-only asserts, comments, or documentation as protective statements. Do not demote a candidate because a callee body is unshown when the callee's standard semantics and the shown arguments already demonstrate the failure; symmetrically, do not attribute nonstandard failure behavior to a callee.

## CWE and severity discipline
The primary CWE names the confirmed mechanism AT THE CONFIRMED SINK; add at most one independently confirmed secondary CWE. When the verdict is not vulnerable, `cwe` is `[]` and severity is `"unknown"` regardless of how concerning the code looked. Prefer the specific class over the generic (CWE-20/119/787) whenever the mechanism is identifiable: CWE-125 for over-read, CWE-787 for over-write, CWE-122 for heap overflow, CWE-121 for stack overflow, CWE-476 for NULL deref, CWE-134 for format string, CWE-195 for a signed value converted to an unsigned size, CWE-190 only when the wrap itself is the root cause (secondary when it merely corrupts a size), CWE-697/CWE-682 for an incorrect comparison that admits a security-relevant boundary, CWE-468 for pointer scaling, CWE-170 for missing string termination. Severity: critical for remote code execution or full auth bypass; high for direct memory corruption or privilege escalation; medium for localized overflow, injection, or leak; low for hardening-level or narrow-condition issues; unknown only when not vulnerable.

Confidence: vulnerable ≥ 0.7 with an exact witness admitted by every shown guard plus a named absent/mutated fix; 0.55–0.7 with a sound residual-range analysis or a fragile-boundary witness; a candidate below 0.5 is demoted to limitations. Not vulnerable ≥ 0.7 with a decisive protective statement quoted with its full excluded set; 0.55–0.7 when safety rests on a complete inventory without a single decisive statement; <= 0.55 when no dangerous operation exists. A confident verdict in either direction is invalid if the corresponding test was skipped or hand-waved.

For conditional-compilation variants, analyze the configuration the shown guards indicate is active; do not claim a missing check inside a branch the shown code excludes.
- Out-of-bounds (CWE-125/122/121/787/119): the capacity must be derivable from the shown fragment — a literal array size, an allocation-size expression, a loop bound over a shown container, a `sizeof` — AND the admitted index or size must exceed it (show the arithmetic). When the sink is a standard API called with shown arguments (memcpy/strcpy/sscanf/printf-family, a read into a buffer the fragment allocated), the callee body need not be shown: the failing condition is derivable from the API's standard semantics plus the shown arguments — an unvalidated attacker-controlled length or count passed to such a call is confirmable at the call site. Symmetrically, do not fabricate an unshown capacity to claim an OOB, and do not refuse a wrapper-sink finding solely because the callee body is unshown.
- Integer overflow / truncation (CWE-190/191/195/681/369): require the arithmetic on shown types, with shown residual ranges, to actually exceed or wrap the type (multiply the admitted maxima; compare widths and signedness at the exact operation). "Product computed before a wider comparison" or "value stored into a narrower field" is a finding only when a shown admitted value demonstrably overflows; mere type widening elsewhere is not. Division: require a shown path that admits divisor == 0.
- Path traversal / symlink (CWE-22/59): a prefix-containment guard (e.g., strncmp over the directory) admits sibling paths only if NO shown statement requires a separator or NUL after the prefix AND every sink consumes the unconstrained value — watch for the guard validating a realpath while the sink opens the original path, and for the boundary test applied to a different string than the sink uses. Name the exact missing boundary character and the sink line.
- Injection / format string (CWE-79/78/89/134/117): a finding requires entry-point-derived content to reach an interpretive sink unvalidated; a literal format with the content passed as data is the safe substitution and resolves the sink PRESENT.
- Status handling (CWE-754/457/252): a discarded or partially-checked status is a candidate, but the failing value must be producible by the shown call under the shown inputs; speculation about unshown callee failure paths is not evidence. An uninitialized read requires a path on which NO shown statement assigns the variable before the read.
- Do not credit debug-only asserts, comments, or documentation as protective statements. Do not demote a candidate because a callee body is unshown when the callee's standard semantics and the shown arguments already demonstrate the failure; symmetrically, do not attribute nonstandard failure behavior to a callee.

## CWE and severity discipline
The primary CWE names the confirmed mechanism AT THE CONFIRMED SINK; add at most one independently confirmed secondary CWE. When the verdict is not vulnerable, `cwe` is `[]` and severity is `"unknown"` regardless of how concerning the code looked. Prefer the specific class over the generic (CWE-20/119/787) whenever the mechanism is identifiable: CWE-125 for over-read, CWE-787 for over-write, CWE-122 for heap overflow, CWE-121 for stack overflow, CWE-476 for NULL deref, CWE-134 for format string, CWE-195 for a signed value converted to an unsigned size, CWE-190 only when the wrap itself is the root cause (secondary when it merely corrupts a size), CWE-697/CWE-682 for an incorrect comparison that admits a security-relevant boundary, CWE-468 for pointer scaling, CWE-170 for missing string termination. Severity: critical for remote code execution or full auth bypass; high for direct memory corruption or privilege escalation; medium for localized overflow, injection, or leak; low for hardening-level or narrow-condition issues; unknown only when not vulnerable.

Confidence: vulnerable ≥ 0.7 with an exact witness admitted by every shown guard plus a named absent/mutated fix; 0.55–0.7 with a sound residual-range analysis or a fragile-boundary witness; a candidate below 0.5 is demoted to limitations. Not vulnerable ≥ 0.7 with a decisive protective statement quoted with its full excluded set; 0.55–0.7 when safety rests on a complete inventory without a single decisive statement; <= 0.55 when no dangerous operation exists. A confident verdict in either direction is invalid if the corresponding test was skipped or hand-waved.

## Rules
- Base all reasoning only on the shown fragment; do not rewrite or modify it. Follow actual control flow (paths, checks, state changes); track real values, types, and exact bounds; quote line numbers and exact operators.
- Membership-identity ban: never argue from which member of the pair the fragment "looks like"; verdicts come only from the Phase 4 Resolution.
- Provenance (Phase 1) decides the residual range to analyze; an unconstrained range alone confirms nothing — the dangerous operation or missing check must actually be in the fragment.
- Ground every safe verdict in protective statements that appear verbatim, execute in the analyzed configuration, and exactly cover the sink's failure set; ground every vulnerable verdict in a capacity, producer, or security context visible in the fragment, a witness admitted by every guard on the path, and a named absent or mutated fix.
- Given the pair structure, expect the one-statement difference to be present, absent, or subtly mutated: audit not just whether a guard exists, but whether its operator, boundary, placement, or constrained variable exactly covers the sink's failure set (the SINGLE-STATEMENT DIFF AUDIT).
- Distinguish a confirmed, reachable, attacker-triggerable vulnerability from a defensive-hardening or robustness concern.
- Do NOT add few-shot examples. Keep the two directions symmetric: every claim in either direction meets the same evidence bar.

## Output format
First: write your SCoT reasoning in plain text with numbered steps (Phases 1–4), explicitly working through Sequence, Branch, and Loop structures, including the per-sink Resolution table and the SINGLE-STATEMENT DIFF AUDIT outcomes for the decisive sink. Keep it concise — 2–6 lines per phase.

Then: output ONLY one JSON object. It must be the LAST thing in your response — no markdown code fences, no text before the first `{`, no text after the closing `}`. The JSON must be complete; do not truncate it.

Required JSON schema (fields and types must match exactly — do not change):
{

    "vulnerable": true/false,
    "confidence": 0.0-1.0,
    "cwe": ["CWE-..."],
    "severity": "low|medium|high|critical|unknown",
    "summary": "..."
  },
  "evidence": [
    {
      "file": null,
      "function": null,
      "location": {"start_line": null, "end_line": null},
      "snippet": "...",
      "reason": "..."
    }
  ],
  "notes": {
    "assumptions": [],
    "limitations": []
  }
}

## Evidence precision requirements
- For each evidence item, set `location.start_line` and `location.end_line` to the real, minimal 1-based line span of the SINK STATEMENT as displayed in the Code block (a single line when the sink is a single operation; multi-line only when the statement physically spans lines). The sink is the FAILING OPERATION itself: for OOB, the indexing/copy statement; for NULL deref, the dereference; for injection, the interpretive call; for a missing status check, the use of the unchecked result; for uninitialized use, the read of the uninitialized object. Never the guard line, the producer, the function header, or a multi-statement range.
- Set `snippet` to the exact code at those lines, quoted verbatim — no paraphrasing, ellipses, substitutions, or comment text.
- SELF-CHECK: after drafting each evidence item, re-read the Code block at the cited lines and confirm the snippet matches character-for-character and the span is minimal; correct any mismatch before output. Multiple distinct sink statements get separate evidence items, with the primary finding's item FIRST — when several sinks resolve ABSENT, the item for the least-protected (deciding) sink comes first.
- Set `reason` to tie the specific index/pointer/size/value to its Phase 1 residual-range source and the Phase 4 confirmed failure, naming the capacity line, the guard's admitted set and its sufficiency or insufficiency (or the mutated form if the guard fails the diff audit), the absent/mutated fix statement, and the primary CWE's mechanism, all INSIDE the reason.
- Keep `notes.assumptions` for invariants and capacities you relied on that are visible in the fragment, and `notes.limitations` for demoted candidates, unconfirmed hypotheses, unshown-environment bypasses, dead witnesses (values blocked by a guard), and out-of-scope concerns.

Code:
do_mouse(
    oparg_T	*oap,		// operator argument, can be NULL
    int		c,		// K_LEFTMOUSE, etc
    int		dir,		// Direction to 'put' if necessary
    long	count,
    int		fixindent)	// PUT_FIXINDENT if fixing indent necessary
{
    static int	do_always = FALSE;	// ignore 'mouse' setting next time
    static int	got_click = FALSE;	// got a click some time back

    int		which_button;	// MOUSE_LEFT, _MIDDLE or _RIGHT
    int		is_click = FALSE; // If FALSE it's a drag or release event
    int		is_drag = FALSE;  // If TRUE it's a drag event
    int		jump_flags = 0;	// flags for jump_to_mouse()
    pos_T	start_visual;
    int		moved;		// Has cursor moved?
    int		in_status_line;	// mouse in status line
    static int	in_tab_line = FALSE; // mouse clicked in tab line
    int		in_sep_line;	// mouse in vertical separator line
    int		c1, c2;
#if defined(FEAT_FOLDING)
    pos_T	save_cursor;
#endif
    win_T	*old_curwin = curwin;
    static pos_T orig_cursor;
    colnr_T	leftcol, rightcol;
    pos_T	end_visual;
    int		diff;
    int		old_active = VIsual_active;
    int		old_mode = VIsual_mode;
    int		regname;

#if defined(FEAT_FOLDING)
    save_cursor = curwin->w_cursor;
#endif

    // When GUI is active, always recognize mouse events, otherwise:
    // - Ignore mouse event in normal mode if 'mouse' doesn't include 'n'.
    // - Ignore mouse event in visual mode if 'mouse' doesn't include 'v'.
    // - For command line and insert mode 'mouse' is checked before calling
    //	 do_mouse().
    if (do_always)
	do_always = FALSE;
    else
#ifdef FEAT_GUI
	if (!gui.in_use)
#endif
	{
	    if (VIsual_active)
	    {
		if (!mouse_has(MOUSE_VISUAL))
		    return FALSE;
	    }
	    else if (State == MODE_NORMAL && !mouse_has(MOUSE_NORMAL))
		return FALSE;
	}

    for (;;)
    {
	which_button = get_mouse_button(KEY2TERMCAP1(c), &is_click, &is_drag);
	if (is_drag)
	{
	    // If the next character is the same mouse event then use that
	    // one. Speeds up dragging the status line.
	    // Note: Since characters added to the stuff buffer in the code
	    // below need to come before the next character, do not do this
	    // when the current character was stuffed.
	    if (!KeyStuffed && vpeekc() != NUL)
	    {
		int nc;
		int save_mouse_row = mouse_row;
		int save_mouse_col = mouse_col;

		// Need to get the character, peeking doesn't get the actual
		// one.
		nc = safe_vgetc();
		if (c == nc)
		    continue;
		vungetc(nc);
		mouse_row = save_mouse_row;
		mouse_col = save_mouse_col;
	    }
	}
	break;
    }

    if (c == K_MOUSEMOVE)
    {
	// Mouse moved without a button pressed.
#ifdef FEAT_BEVAL_TERM
	ui_may_remove_balloon();
	if (p_bevalterm)
	{
	    profile_setlimit(p_bdlay, &bevalexpr_due);
	    bevalexpr_due_set = TRUE;
	}
#endif
#ifdef FEAT_PROP_POPUP
	popup_handle_mouse_moved();
#endif
	return FALSE;
    }

#ifdef FEAT_MOUSESHAPE
    // May have stopped dragging the status or separator line.  The pointer is
    // most likely still on the status or separator line.
    if (!is_drag && drag_status_line)
    {
	drag_status_line = FALSE;
	update_mouseshape(SHAPE_IDX_STATUS);
    }
    if (!is_drag && drag_sep_line)
    {
	drag_sep_line = FALSE;
	update_mouseshape(SHAPE_IDX_VSEP);
    }
#endif

    // Ignore drag and release events if we didn't get a click.
    if (is_click)
	got_click = TRUE;
    else
    {
	if (!got_click)			// didn't get click, ignore
	    return FALSE;
	if (!is_drag)			// release, reset got_click
	{
	    got_click = FALSE;
	    if (in_tab_line)
	    {
		in_tab_line = FALSE;
		return FALSE;
	    }
	}
    }

    // CTRL right mouse button does CTRL-T
    if (is_click && (mod_mask & MOD_MASK_CTRL) && which_button == MOUSE_RIGHT)
    {
	if (State & MODE_INSERT)
	    stuffcharReadbuff(Ctrl_O);
	if (count > 1)
	    stuffnumReadbuff(count);
	stuffcharReadbuff(Ctrl_T);
	got_click = FALSE;		// ignore drag&release now
	return FALSE;
    }

    // CTRL only works with left mouse button
    if ((mod_mask & MOD_MASK_CTRL) && which_button != MOUSE_LEFT)
	return FALSE;

    // When a modifier is down, ignore drag and release events, as well as
    // multiple clicks and the middle mouse button.
    // Accept shift-leftmouse drags when 'mousemodel' is "popup.*".
    if ((mod_mask & (MOD_MASK_SHIFT | MOD_MASK_CTRL | MOD_MASK_ALT
							     | MOD_MASK_META))
	    && (!is_click
		|| (mod_mask & MOD_MASK_MULTI_CLICK)
		|| which_button == MOUSE_MIDDLE)
	    && !((mod_mask & (MOD_MASK_SHIFT|MOD_MASK_ALT))
		&& mouse_model_popup()
		&& which_button == MOUSE_LEFT)
	    && !((mod_mask & MOD_MASK_ALT)
		&& !mouse_model_popup()
		&& which_button == MOUSE_RIGHT)
	    )
	return FALSE;

    // If the button press was used as the movement command for an operator
    // (eg "d<MOUSE>"), or it is the middle button that is held down, ignore
    // drag/release events.
    if (!is_click && which_button == MOUSE_MIDDLE)
	return FALSE;

    if (oap != NULL)
	regname = oap->regname;
    else
	regname = 0;

    // Middle mouse button does a 'put' of the selected text
    if (which_button == MOUSE_MIDDLE)
    {
	if (State == MODE_NORMAL)
	{
	    // If an operator was pending, we don't know what the user wanted
	    // to do. Go back to normal mode: Clear the operator and beep().
	    if (oap != NULL && oap->op_type != OP_NOP)
	    {
		clearopbeep(oap);
		return FALSE;
	    }

	    // If visual was active, yank the highlighted text and put it
	    // before the mouse pointer position.
	    // In Select mode replace the highlighted text with the clipboard.
	    if (VIsual_active)
	    {
		if (VIsual_select)
		{
		    stuffcharReadbuff(Ctrl_G);
		    stuffReadbuff((char_u *)"\"+p");
		}
		else
		{
		    stuffcharReadbuff('y');
		    stuffcharReadbuff(K_MIDDLEMOUSE);
		}
		do_always = TRUE;	// ignore 'mouse' setting next time
		return FALSE;
	    }
	    // The rest is below jump_to_mouse()
	}

	else if ((State & MODE_INSERT) == 0)
	    return FALSE;

	// Middle click in insert mode doesn't move the mouse, just insert the
	// contents of a register.  '.' register is special, can't insert that
	// with do_put().
	// Also paste at the cursor if the current mode isn't in 'mouse' (only
	// happens for the GUI).
	if ((State & MODE_INSERT) || !mouse_has(MOUSE_NORMAL))
	{
	    if (regname == '.')
		insert_reg(regname, TRUE);
	    else
	    {
#ifdef FEAT_CLIPBOARD
		if (clip_star.available && regname == 0)
		    regname = '*';
#endif
		if ((State & REPLACE_FLAG) && !yank_register_mline(regname))
		    insert_reg(regname, TRUE);
		else
		{
		    do_put(regname, NULL, BACKWARD, 1L,
						      fixindent | PUT_CURSEND);

		    // Repeat it with CTRL-R CTRL-O r or CTRL-R CTRL-P r
		    AppendCharToRedobuff(Ctrl_R);
		    AppendCharToRedobuff(fixindent ? Ctrl_P : Ctrl_O);
		    AppendCharToRedobuff(regname == 0 ? '"' : regname);
		}
	    }
	    return FALSE;
	}
    }

    // When dragging or button-up stay in the same window.
    if (!is_click)
	jump_flags |= MOUSE_FOCUS | MOUSE_DID_MOVE;

    start_visual.lnum = 0;

    if (TabPageIdxs != NULL)  // only when initialized
    {
	// Check for clicking in the tab page line.
	if (mouse_row == 0 && firstwin->w_winrow > 0)
	{
	    if (is_drag)
	    {
		if (in_tab_line)
		{
		    c1 = TabPageIdxs[mouse_col];
		    tabpage_move(c1 <= 0 ? 9999 : c1 < tabpage_index(curtab)
								    ? c1 - 1 : c1);
		}
		return FALSE;
	    }

	    // click in a tab selects that tab page
	    if (is_click
# ifdef FEAT_CMDWIN
		    && cmdwin_type == 0
# endif
		    && mouse_col < Columns)
	    {
		in_tab_line = TRUE;
		c1 = TabPageIdxs[mouse_col];
		if (c1 >= 0)
		{
		    if ((mod_mask & MOD_MASK_MULTI_CLICK) == MOD_MASK_2CLICK)
		    {
			// double click opens new page
			end_visual_mode_keep_button();
			tabpage_new();
			tabpage_move(c1 == 0 ? 9999 : c1 - 1);
		    }
		    else
		    {
			// Go to specified tab page, or next one if not clicking
			// on a label.
			goto_tabpage(c1);

			// It's like clicking on the status line of a window.
			if (curwin != old_curwin)
			    end_visual_mode_keep_button();
		    }
		}
		else
		{
		    tabpage_T	*tp;

		    // Close the current or specified tab page.
		    if (c1 == -999)
			tp = curtab;
		    else
			tp = find_tabpage(-c1);
		    if (tp == curtab)
		    {
			if (first_tabpage->tp_next != NULL)
			    tabpage_close(FALSE);
		    }
		    else if (tp != NULL)
			tabpage_close_other(tp, FALSE);
		}
	    }
	    return TRUE;
	}
	else if (is_drag && in_tab_line)
	{
	    c1 = TabPageIdxs[mouse_col];
	    tabpage_move(c1 <= 0 ? 9999 : c1 - 1);
	    return FALSE;
	}
    }

    // When 'mousemodel' is "popup" or "popup_setpos", translate mouse events:
    // right button up   -> pop-up menu
    // shift-left button -> right button
    // alt-left button   -> alt-right button
    if (mouse_model_popup())
    {
	if (which_button == MOUSE_RIGHT
			    && !(mod_mask & (MOD_MASK_SHIFT | MOD_MASK_CTRL)))
	{
#ifdef USE_POPUP_SETPOS
# ifdef FEAT_GUI
	    if (gui.in_use)
	    {
#  if defined(FEAT_GUI_MOTIF) || defined(FEAT_GUI_GTK) \
			  || defined(FEAT_GUI_PHOTON)
		if (!is_click)
		    // Ignore right button release events, only shows the popup
		    // menu on the button down event.
		    return FALSE;
#  endif
#  if defined(FEAT_GUI_MSWIN) || defined(FEAT_GUI_HAIKU)
		if (is_click || is_drag)
		    // Ignore right button down and drag mouse events.  Windows
		    // only shows the popup menu on the button up event.
		    return FALSE;
#  endif
	    }
# endif
# if defined(FEAT_GUI) && defined(FEAT_TERM_POPUP_MENU)
	    else
# endif
# if defined(FEAT_TERM_POPUP_MENU)
	    if (!is_click)
		// Ignore right button release events, only shows the popup
		// menu on the button down event.
		return FALSE;
#endif

	    jump_flags = 0;
	    if (STRCMP(p_mousem, "popup_setpos") == 0)
	    {
		// First set the cursor position before showing the popup
		// menu.
		if (VIsual_active)
		{
		    pos_T    m_pos;

		    // set MOUSE_MAY_STOP_VIS if we are outside the
		    // selection or the current window (might have false
		    // negative here)
		    if (mouse_row < curwin->w_winrow
			 || mouse_row
				  > (curwin->w_winrow + curwin->w_height))
			jump_flags = MOUSE_MAY_STOP_VIS;
		    else if (get_fpos_of_mouse(&m_pos) != IN_BUFFER)
			jump_flags = MOUSE_MAY_STOP_VIS;
		    else
		    {
			if ((LT_POS(curwin->w_cursor, VIsual)
				    && (LT_POS(m_pos, curwin->w_cursor)
					|| LT_POS(VIsual, m_pos)))
				|| (LT_POS(VIsual, curwin->w_cursor)
				    && (LT_POS(m_pos, VIsual)
				      || LT_POS(curwin->w_cursor, m_pos))))
			{
			    jump_flags = MOUSE_MAY_STOP_VIS;
			}
			else if (VIsual_mode == Ctrl_V)
			{
			    getvcols(curwin, &curwin->w_cursor, &VIsual,
						     &leftcol, &rightcol);
			    getvcol(curwin, &m_pos, NULL, &m_pos.col, NULL);
			    if (m_pos.col < leftcol || m_pos.col > rightcol)
				jump_flags = MOUSE_MAY_STOP_VIS;
			}
		    }
		}
		else
		    jump_flags = MOUSE_MAY_STOP_VIS;
	    }
	    if (jump_flags)
	    {
		jump_flags = jump_to_mouse(jump_flags, NULL, which_button);
		update_curbuf(VIsual_active ? UPD_INVERTED : UPD_VALID);
		setcursor();
		out_flush();    // Update before showing popup menu
	    }
# ifdef FEAT_MENU
	    show_popupmenu();
	    got_click = FALSE;	// ignore release events
# endif
	    return (jump_flags & CURSOR_MOVED) != 0;
#else
	    return FALSE;
#endif
	}
	if (which_button == MOUSE_LEFT
				&& (mod_mask & (MOD_MASK_SHIFT|MOD_MASK_ALT)))
	{
	    which_button = MOUSE_RIGHT;
	    mod_mask &= ~MOD_MASK_SHIFT;
	}
    }

    if ((State & (MODE_NORMAL | MODE_INSERT))
			    && !(mod_mask & (MOD_MASK_SHIFT | MOD_MASK_CTRL)))
    {
	if (which_button == MOUSE_LEFT)
	{
	    if (is_click)
	    {
		// stop Visual mode for a left click in a window, but not when
		// on a status line
		if (VIsual_active)
		    jump_flags |= MOUSE_MAY_STOP_VIS;
	    }
	    else if (mouse_has(MOUSE_VISUAL))
		jump_flags |= MOUSE_MAY_VIS;
	}
	else if (which_button == MOUSE_RIGHT)
	{
	    if (is_click && VIsual_active)
	    {
		// Remember the start and end of visual before moving the
		// cursor.
		if (LT_POS(curwin->w_cursor, VIsual))
		{
		    start_visual = curwin->w_cursor;
		    end_visual = VIsual;
		}
		else
		{
		    start_visual = VIsual;
		    end_visual = curwin->w_cursor;
		}
	    }
	    jump_flags |= MOUSE_FOCUS;
	    if (mouse_has(MOUSE_VISUAL))
		jump_flags |= MOUSE_MAY_VIS;
	}
    }

    // If an operator is pending, ignore all drags and releases until the
    // next mouse click.
    if (!is_drag && oap != NULL && oap->op_type != OP_NOP)
    {
	got_click = FALSE;
	oap->motion_type = MCHAR;
    }

    // When releasing the button let jump_to_mouse() know.
    if (!is_click && !is_drag)
	jump_flags |= MOUSE_RELEASED;

    // JUMP!
    jump_flags = jump_to_mouse(jump_flags,
			oap == NULL ? NULL : &(oap->inclusive), which_button);

#ifdef FEAT_MENU
    // A click in the window toolbar has no side effects.
    if (jump_flags & MOUSE_WINBAR)
	return FALSE;
#endif
    moved = (jump_flags & CURSOR_MOVED);
    in_status_line = (jump_flags & IN_STATUS_LINE);
    in_sep_line = (jump_flags & IN_SEP_LINE);

#ifdef FEAT_NETBEANS_INTG
    if (isNetbeansBuffer(curbuf)
			    && !(jump_flags & (IN_STATUS_LINE | IN_SEP_LINE)))
    {
	int key = KEY2TERMCAP1(c);

	if (key == (int)KE_LEFTRELEASE || key == (int)KE_MIDDLERELEASE
					       || key == (int)KE_RIGHTRELEASE)
	    netbeans_button_release(which_button);
    }
#endif

    // When jumping to another window, clear a pending operator.  That's a bit
    // friendlier than beeping and not jumping to that window.
    if (curwin != old_curwin && oap != NULL && oap->op_type != OP_NOP)
	clearop(oap);

#ifdef FEAT_FOLDING
    if (mod_mask == 0
	    && !is_drag
	    && (jump_flags & (MOUSE_FOLD_CLOSE | MOUSE_FOLD_OPEN))
	    && which_button == MOUSE_LEFT)
    {
	// open or close a fold at this line
	if (jump_flags & MOUSE_FOLD_OPEN)
	    openFold(curwin->w_cursor.lnum, 1L);
	else
	    closeFold(curwin->w_cursor.lnum, 1L);
	// don't move the cursor if still in the same window
	if (curwin == old_curwin)
	    curwin->w_cursor = save_cursor;

   - REACH: the guard executes on EVERY path to the sink — including alternate branches, loop-carried paths, and early-return exits — and is not skipped, compiled out, or debug-only;
   - EXACTNESS: the operator, boundary constant, and constrained variable exactly cover the failure set (no off-by-one, no `>` where `>=` is needed, no wrong variable, no too-large boundary, no check on a sanitized copy while the sink consumes the original).
3. SINGLE-STATEMENT DIFF AUDIT: for each fix candidate, mutate it by one token — reverse the operator, shift the boundary by ±1, swap the constrained variable for a sibling, move the check after the sink, drop the boundary-character test — and ask whether an admitted value then reaches the sink. Three outcomes:
   - the shown guard equals the correct protective form → PRESENT;
   - the shown guard equals the mutated (broken) form → ABSENT, and the admitted boundary value is the witness (name it);
   - the shown guard is absent where the sink needs one → ABSENT (missing fix).
   This audit targets the one-statement difference directly: the fragment carries either the correct statement or its broken/missing form.

### Phase 3 — Loop: bounds, induction, and capacity consistency
For every loop feeding a sink: state the loop bounds in terms of the actual variables, the type and provenance of the index/counter, every exit path (condition fail, break, continue, return), and the capacity of the accessed object. Prove or disprove by induction that every iteration index stays inside the shown capacity; check the first and last iterations explicitly. Check capacity consistency across statements: the allocation size, the write/copy size, and the loop bound must match under the shown types (signedness and element size included). A loop whose bound is attacker-derived and never checked against the object's capacity is a candidate; a loop whose bound exactly matches a shown capacity resolves PRESENT only if the capacity statement is actually shown and no path makes the index negative or the count exceed it.

### Phase 4 — Resolution and verdict
Produce the per-sink Resolution table: for EVERY dangerous operation from Phase 1, one row — sink line, failure set, PRESENT (protective statement verbatim + the exact values it excludes) or ABSENT (missing/mutated fix + the surviving witness), and whether that row is decisive. If ANY sink resolves ABSENT, the verdict is vulnerable, even if other sinks are PRESENT; order the evidence with the least-protected (deciding) sink FIRST. If every sink resolves PRESENT with a statement that survives Phases 2–3, the verdict is not vulnerable — absence of a demonstrated flaw is a weaker verdict, not a stronger one; a safe verdict requires the protective statement, not merely the absence of a proof of harm. End with a one-line verdict justification quoting the decisive statement or witness.

## Evidence standards (apply symmetrically in both directions)
- NULL dereference (CWE-476): a finding requires a NULL value that is PRODUCED or ADMITTED by shown statements — a NULL-initialized variable assigned from a shown call with standard NULL-on-failure semantics, or a guard that admits a NULL state — plus a shown dereference on a path that reaches that NULL unexcluded. "Library routine may return NULL on OOM", "a field may be NULL in some OS state", and "a sibling pointer is NULL-checked, so this one might be NULL too" are NOT by themselves findings. For conditional-compilation variants, analyze the configuration the shown guards indicate is active; do not claim a missing check inside a branch the shown code excludes.
- Out-of-bounds (CWE-125/122/121/787/119): the capacity must be derivable from the shown fragment — a literal array size, an allocation-size expression, a loop bound over a shown container, a `sizeof` — AND the admitted index or size must exceed it (show the arithmetic). When the sink is a standard API called with shown arguments (memcpy/strcpy/sscanf/printf-family, a read into a buffer the fragment allocated), the callee body need not be shown: the failing condition is derivable from the API's standard semantics plus the shown arguments — an unvalidated attacker-controlled length or count passed to such a call is confirmable at the call site. Symmetrically, do not fabricate an unshown capacity to claim an OOB, and do not refuse a wrapper-sink finding solely because the callee body is unshown.
- Integer overflow / truncation (CWE-190/191/195/681/369): require the arithmetic on shown types, with shown residual ranges, to actually exceed or wrap the type (multiply the admitted maxima; compare widths and signedness at the exact operation). "Product computed before a wider comparison" or "value stored into a narrower field" is a finding only when a shown admitted value demonstrably overflows; mere type widening elsewhere is not. Division: require a shown path that admits divisor == 0.
- Path traversal / symlink (CWE-22/59): a prefix-containment guard (e.g., strncmp over the directory) admits sibling paths only if NO shown statement requires a separator or NUL after the prefix AND every sink consumes the unconstrained value — watch for the guard validating a realpath while the sink opens the original path, and for the boundary test applied to a different string than the sink uses. Name the exact missing boundary character and the sink line.
- Injection / format string (CWE-79/78/89/134/117): a finding requires entry-point-derived content to reach an interpretive sink unvalidated; a literal format with the content passed as data is the safe substitution and resolves the sink PRESENT.
- Status handling (CWE-754/457/252): a discarded or partially-checked status is a candidate, but the failing value must be producible by the shown call under the shown inputs; speculation about unshown callee failure paths is not evidence. An uninitialized read requires a path on which NO shown statement assigns the variable before the read.
- Do not credit debug-only asserts, comments, or documentation as protective statements. Do not demote a candidate because a callee body is unshown when the callee's standard semantics and the shown arguments already demonstrate the failure; symmetrically, do not attribute nonstandard failure behavior to a callee.

## CWE and severity discipline
The primary CWE names the confirmed mechanism AT THE CONFIRMED SINK; add at most one independently confirmed secondary CWE. When the verdict is not vulnerable, `cwe` is `[]` and severity is `"unknown"` regardless of how concerning the code looked. Prefer the specific class over the generic (CWE-20/119/787) whenever the mechanism is identifiable: CWE-125 for over-read, CWE-787 for over-write, CWE-122 for heap overflow, CWE-121 for stack overflow, CWE-476 for NULL deref, CWE-134 for format string, CWE-195 for a signed value converted to an unsigned size, CWE-190 only when the wrap itself is the root cause (secondary when it merely corrupts a size), CWE-697/CWE-682 for an incorrect comparison that admits a security-relevant boundary, CWE-468 for pointer scaling, CWE-170 for missing string termination. Severity: critical for remote code execution or full auth bypass; high for direct memory corruption or privilege escalation; medium for localized overflow, injection, or leak; low for hardening-level or narrow-condition issues; unknown only when not vulnerable.

Confidence: vulnerable ≥ 0.7 with an exact witness admitted by every shown guard plus a named absent/mutated fix; 0.55–0.7 with a sound residual-range analysis or a fragile-boundary witness; a candidate below 0.5 is demoted to limitations. Not vulnerable ≥ 0.7 with a decisive protective statement quoted with its full excluded set; 0.55–0.7 when safety rests on a complete inventory without a single decisive statement; <= 0.55 when no dangerous operation exists. A confident verdict in either direction is invalid if the corresponding test was skipped or hand-waved.

## Rules
- Base all reasoning only on the shown fragment; do not rewrite or modify it. Follow actual control flow (paths, checks, state changes); track real values, types, and exact bounds; quote line numbers and exact operators.
- Membership-identity ban: never argue from which member of the pair the fragment "looks like"; verdicts come only from the Phase 4 Resolution.
- Provenance (Phase 1) decides the residual range to analyze; an unconstrained range alone confirms nothing — the dangerous operation or missing check must actually be in the fragment.
- Ground every safe verdict in protective statements that appear verbatim, execute in the analyzed configuration, and exactly cover the sink's failure set; ground every vulnerable verdict in a capacity, producer, or security context visible in the fragment, a witness admitted by every guard on the path, and a named absent or mutated fix.
- Given the pair structure, expect the one-statement difference to be present, absent, or subtly mutated: audit not just whether a guard exists, but whether its operator, boundary, placement, or constrained variable exactly covers the sink's failure set (the SINGLE-STATEMENT DIFF AUDIT).
- Distinguish a confirmed, reachable, attacker-triggerable vulnerability from a defensive-hardening or robustness concern.
- Do NOT add few-shot examples. Keep the two directions symmetric: every claim in either direction meets the same evidence bar.

## Output format
First: write your SCoT reasoning in plain text with numbered steps (Phases 1–4), explicitly working through Sequence, Branch, and Loop structures, including the per-sink Resolution table and the SINGLE-STATEMENT DIFF AUDIT outcomes for the decisive sink. Keep it concise — 2–6 lines per phase.

Then: output ONLY one JSON object. It must be the LAST thing in your response — no markdown code fences, no text before the first `{`, no text after the closing `}`. The JSON must be complete; do not truncate it.

Required JSON schema (fields and types must match exactly — do not change):
{
  "verdict": {
    "vulnerable": true/false,
    "confidence": 0.0-1.0,
    "cwe": ["CWE-..."],
    "severity": "low|medium|high|critical|unknown",
    "summary": "..."
  },
  "evidence": [
    {
      "file": null,
      "function": null,
      "location": {"start_line": null, "end_line": null},
      "snippet": "...",
      "reason": "..."
    }
  ],
  "notes": {
    "assumptions": [],
    "limitations": []
  }
}

## Evidence precision requirements
- For each evidence item, set `location.start_line` and `location.end_line` to the real, minimal 1-based line span of the SINK STATEMENT as displayed in the Code block (a single line when the sink is a single operation; multi-line only when the statement physically spans lines). The sink is the FAILING OPERATION itself: for OOB, the indexing/copy statement; for NULL deref, the dereference; for injection, the interpretive call; for a missing status check, the use of the unchecked result; for uninitialized use, the read of the uninitialized object. Never the guard line, the producer, the function header, or a multi-statement range.
- Set `snippet` to the exact code at those lines, quoted verbatim — no paraphrasing, ellipses, substitutions, or comment text.
- SELF-CHECK: after drafting each evidence item, re-read the Code block at the cited lines and confirm the snippet matches character-for-character and the span is minimal; correct any mismatch before output. Multiple distinct sink statements get separate evidence items, with the primary finding's item FIRST — when several sinks resolve ABSENT, the item for the least-protected (deciding) sink comes first.
- Set `reason` to tie the specific index/pointer/size/value to its Phase 1 residual-range source and the Phase 4 confirmed failure, naming the capacity line, the guard's admitted set and its sufficiency or insufficiency (or the mutated form if the guard fails the diff audit), the absent/mutated fix statement, and the primary CWE's mechanism, all INSIDE the reason.
- Keep `notes.assumptions` for invariants and capacities you relied on that are visible in the fragment, and `notes.limitations` for demoted candidates, unconfirmed hypotheses, unshown-environment bypasses, dead witnesses (values blocked by a guard), and out-of-scope concerns.

Code:
negotiate_handshake_newstyle_options (void)
{
  GET_CONN;
  struct nbd_new_option new_option;
  size_t nr_options;
  bool list_seen = false;
  uint64_t version;
  uint32_t option;
  uint32_t optlen;
  struct nbd_export_name_option_reply handshake_finish;
  const char *optname;
  uint64_t exportsize;
  struct backend *b;

  for (nr_options = MAX_NR_OPTIONS; nr_options > 0; --nr_options) {
    CLEANUP_FREE char *data = NULL;

    if (conn_recv_full (&new_option, sizeof new_option,
                        "reading option: conn->recv: %m") == -1)
      return -1;

    version = be64toh (new_option.version);
    if (version != NBD_NEW_VERSION) {
      nbdkit_error ("unknown option version %" PRIx64
                    ", expecting %" PRIx64,
                    version, NBD_NEW_VERSION);
      return -1;
    }

    /* There is a maximum option length we will accept, regardless
     * of the option type.
     */
    optlen = be32toh (new_option.optlen);
    if (optlen > MAX_REQUEST_SIZE) {
      nbdkit_error ("client option data too long (%" PRIu32 ")", optlen);
      return -1;
    }
    data = malloc (optlen + 1); /* Allowing a trailing NUL helps some uses */
    if (data == NULL) {
      nbdkit_error ("malloc: %m");
      return -1;
    }

    option = be32toh (new_option.option);
    optname = name_of_nbd_opt (option);

    /* If the client lacks fixed newstyle support, it should only send
     * NBD_OPT_EXPORT_NAME.
     */
    if (!(conn->cflags & NBD_FLAG_FIXED_NEWSTYLE) &&
        option != NBD_OPT_EXPORT_NAME) {
      if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID))
        return -1;
      continue;
    }

    /* In --tls=require / FORCEDTLS mode the only options allowed
     * before TLS negotiation are NBD_OPT_ABORT and NBD_OPT_STARTTLS.
     */
    if (tls == 2 && !conn->using_tls &&
        !(option == NBD_OPT_ABORT || option == NBD_OPT_STARTTLS)) {
      if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_TLS_REQD))
        return -1;
      continue;
    }

    switch (option) {
    case NBD_OPT_EXPORT_NAME:
      if (conn_recv_full (data, optlen,
                          "read: %s: %m", name_of_nbd_opt (option)) == -1)
        return -1;
      if (check_export_name (option, data, optlen, optlen) == -1)
        return -1;

      /* We have to finish the handshake by sending handshake_finish.
       * On failure, we have to disconnect.
       */
      if (finish_newstyle_options (&exportsize, data, optlen) == -1)
        return -1;

      memset (&handshake_finish, 0, sizeof handshake_finish);
      handshake_finish.exportsize = htobe64 (exportsize);
      handshake_finish.eflags = htobe16 (conn->eflags);

      if (conn->send (&handshake_finish,
                      (conn->cflags & NBD_FLAG_NO_ZEROES)
                      ? offsetof (struct nbd_export_name_option_reply, zeroes)
                      : sizeof handshake_finish, 0) == -1) {
        nbdkit_error ("write: %s: %m", optname);
        return -1;
      }
      break;

    case NBD_OPT_ABORT:
      if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ACK) == -1)
        return -1;
      debug ("client sent %s to abort the connection",
             name_of_nbd_opt (option));
      return -1;

    case NBD_OPT_LIST:
      if (optlen != 0) {
        if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID)
            == -1)
          return -1;
        if (conn_recv_full (data, optlen,
                            "read: %s: %m", name_of_nbd_opt (option)) == -1)
          return -1;
        continue;
      }

      if (list_seen) {
        debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: export list already advertised",
               name_of_nbd_opt (option));
        if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID) == -1)
          return -1;
        continue;
      }
      else {
        /* Send back the exportname list. */
        debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: advertising exports",
               name_of_nbd_opt (option));
        if (send_newstyle_option_reply_exportnames (option, &nr_options) == -1)
          return -1;
        list_seen = true;
      }
      break;

    case NBD_OPT_STARTTLS:
      if (optlen != 0) {
        if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID)
            == -1)
          return -1;
        if (conn_recv_full (data, optlen,
                            "read: %s: %m", name_of_nbd_opt (option)) == -1)
          return -1;
        continue;
      }

      if (tls == 0) {           /* --tls=off (NOTLS mode). */
#ifdef HAVE_GNUTLS
#define NO_TLS_REPLY NBD_REP_ERR_POLICY
#else
#define NO_TLS_REPLY NBD_REP_ERR_UNSUP
#endif
        if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NO_TLS_REPLY) == -1)
          return -1;
      }
      else /* --tls=on or --tls=require */ {
        /* We can't upgrade to TLS twice on the same connection. */
        if (conn->using_tls) {
          if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID) == -1)
            return -1;
          continue;
        }

        /* We have to send the (unencrypted) reply before starting
         * the handshake.
         */
        if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ACK) == -1)
          return -1;

        /* Upgrade the connection to TLS.  Also performs access control. */
        if (crypto_negotiate_tls (conn->sockin, conn->sockout) == -1)
          return -1;
        conn->using_tls = true;
        debug ("using TLS on this connection");
        /* Wipe out any cached state. */
        conn->structured_replies = false;
        for_each_backend (b) {
          free (conn->default_exportname[b->i]);
          conn->default_exportname[b->i] = NULL;
        }
      }
      break;

    case NBD_OPT_INFO:
    case NBD_OPT_GO:
      if (conn_recv_full (data, optlen, "read: %s: %m", optname) == -1)
        return -1;

      if (optlen < 6) { /* 32 bit export length + 16 bit nr info */
        debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s option length < 6", optname);

        if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID)
            == -1)
          return -1;
        continue;
      }

      {
        uint32_t exportnamelen;
        uint16_t nrinfos;
        uint16_t info;
        size_t i;

        /* Validate the name length and number of INFO requests. */
        memcpy (&exportnamelen, &data[0], 4);
        exportnamelen = be32toh (exportnamelen);
        if (exportnamelen > optlen-6 /* NB optlen >= 6, see above */) {
          debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: export name too long", optname);
          if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID)
              == -1)
            return -1;
          continue;
        }
        memcpy (&nrinfos, &data[exportnamelen+4], 2);
        nrinfos = be16toh (nrinfos);
        if (optlen != 4 + exportnamelen + 2 + 2*nrinfos) {
          debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: "
                 "number of information requests incorrect", optname);
          if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID)
              == -1)
            return -1;
          continue;
        }

        /* As with NBD_OPT_EXPORT_NAME we print the export name and
         * save it in the connection.  If an earlier
         * NBD_OPT_SET_META_CONTEXT used an export name, it must match
         * or else we drop the support for that context.
         */
        if (check_export_name (option, &data[4], exportnamelen,
                               optlen - 6) == -1) {
          if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID)
              == -1)
            return -1;
          continue;
        }

        /* The spec is confusing, but it is required that we send back
         * NBD_INFO_EXPORT, even if the client did not request it!
         * qemu client in particular does not request this, but will
         * fail if we don't send it.  Note that if .open fails, but we
         * succeed at .close, then we merely return an error to the
         * client and let them try another NBD_OPT, rather than
         * disconnecting.
         */
        if (finish_newstyle_options (&exportsize,
                                     &data[4], exportnamelen) == -1) {
          if (conn->top_context) {
            if (backend_finalize (conn->top_context) == -1)
              return -1;
            backend_close (conn->top_context);
            conn->top_context = NULL;
          }
          if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_UNKNOWN) == -1)
            return -1;
          continue;
        }

        if (send_newstyle_option_reply_info_export (option,
                                                    NBD_REP_INFO,
                                                    NBD_INFO_EXPORT,
                                                    exportsize) == -1)
          return -1;

        /* For now we send NBD_INFO_NAME and NBD_INFO_DESCRIPTION if
         * requested, and ignore all other info requests (including
         * NBD_INFO_EXPORT if it was requested, because we replied
         * already above).
         */
        for (i = 0; i < nrinfos; ++i) {
          memcpy (&info, &data[4 + exportnamelen + 2 + i*2], 2);
          info = be16toh (info);
          switch (info) {
          case NBD_INFO_EXPORT: /* ignore - reply sent above */ break;
          case NBD_INFO_NAME:
            {
              const char *name = &data[4];
              size_t namelen = exportnamelen;

              if (exportnamelen == 0) {
                name = backend_default_export (top, read_only);
                if (!name) {
                  debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: "
                         "NBD_INFO_NAME: no name to send", optname);
                  break;
                }
                namelen = -1;
              }
              if (send_newstyle_option_reply_info_str (option,
                                                       NBD_REP_INFO,
                                                       NBD_INFO_NAME,
                                                       name, namelen) == -1)
                return -1;
            }
            break;
          case NBD_INFO_DESCRIPTION:
            {
              const char *desc = backend_export_description (conn->top_context);

              if (!desc) {
                debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: "
                       "NBD_INFO_DESCRIPTION: no description to send",
                       optname);
                break;
              }
              if (send_newstyle_option_reply_info_str (option,
                                                       NBD_REP_INFO,
                                                       NBD_INFO_DESCRIPTION,
                                                       desc, -1) == -1)
                return -1;
            }
            break;
          default:
            debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: "
                   "ignoring NBD_INFO_* request %u (%s)",
                   optname, (unsigned) info, name_of_nbd_info (info));
            break;
          }
        }
      }

      /* Unlike NBD_OPT_EXPORT_NAME, NBD_OPT_GO sends back an ACK
       * or ERROR packet.  If this was NBD_OPT_LIST, call .close.
       */
      if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ACK) == -1)
        return -1;

      if (option == NBD_OPT_INFO) {
        if (backend_finalize (conn->top_context) == -1)
          return -1;
        backend_close (conn->top_context);
        conn->top_context = NULL;
      }

      break;

    case NBD_OPT_STRUCTURED_REPLY:
      if (optlen != 0) {
        if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID)
            == -1)
          return -1;
        if (conn_recv_full (data, optlen,
                            "read: %s: %m", name_of_nbd_opt (option)) == -1)
          return -1;
        continue;
      }

      debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: client requested structured replies",
             name_of_nbd_opt (option));

      if (no_sr) {
        /* Must fail with ERR_UNSUP for qemu 4.2 to remain happy;
         * but failing with ERR_POLICY would have been nicer.
         */
        if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_UNSUP) == -1)
          return -1;
        debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: structured replies are disabled",
               name_of_nbd_opt (option));
        break;
      }

      if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ACK) == -1)
        return -1;

      conn->structured_replies = true;
      break;

    case NBD_OPT_LIST_META_CONTEXT:
    case NBD_OPT_SET_META_CONTEXT:
      {
        uint32_t opt_index;
        uint32_t exportnamelen;
        uint32_t nr_queries;
        uint32_t querylen;
        const char *what;

        if (conn_recv_full (data, optlen, "read: %s: %m", optname) == -1)
          return -1;

        /* Note that we support base:allocation whether or not the plugin
         * supports can_extents.
         */
        if (!conn->structured_replies) {
          if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID)
              == -1)
            return -1;
          continue;
        }

        /* Minimum length of the option payload is:
         *   32 bit export name length followed by empty export name
         * + 32 bit number of queries followed by no queries
         * = 8 bytes.
         */
        what = "optlen < 8";
        if (optlen < 8) {
        opt_meta_invalid_option_len:
          debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: invalid option length: %s",
                 optname, what);

          if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ERR_INVALID)
              == -1)
            return -1;
          continue;
        }

        memcpy (&exportnamelen, &data[0], 4);
        exportnamelen = be32toh (exportnamelen);
        what = "validating export name";
        if (check_export_name (option, &data[4], exportnamelen,
                               optlen - 8) == -1)
          goto opt_meta_invalid_option_len;

        /* Remember the export name: the NBD spec says that if the client
         * later uses NBD_OPT_GO on a different export, then the context
         * returned here is not usable.
         */
        if (option == NBD_OPT_SET_META_CONTEXT) {
          conn->exportname_from_set_meta_context =
            strndup (&data[4], exportnamelen);
          if (conn->exportname_from_set_meta_context == NULL) {
            nbdkit_error ("malloc: %m");
            return -1;
          }
        }

        opt_index = 4 + exportnamelen;

        /* Read the number of queries. */
        what = "reading number of queries";
        if (opt_index+4 > optlen)
          goto opt_meta_invalid_option_len;
        memcpy (&nr_queries, &data[opt_index], 4);
        nr_queries = be32toh (nr_queries);
        opt_index += 4;

        /* for LIST: nr_queries == 0 means return all meta contexts
         * for SET: nr_queries == 0 means reset all contexts
         */
        debug ("newstyle negotiation: %s: %s count: %d", optname,
               option == NBD_OPT_LIST_META_CONTEXT ? "query" : "set",
               nr_queries);
        if (option == NBD_OPT_SET_META_CONTEXT)
          conn->meta_context_base_allocation = false;
        if (nr_queries == 0) {
          if (option == NBD_OPT_LIST_META_CONTEXT) {
            if (send_newstyle_option_reply_meta_context (option,
                                                         NBD_REP_META_CONTEXT,
                                                         0, "base:allocation")
                == -1)
              return -1;
          }

          if (send_newstyle_option_reply (option, NBD_REP_ACK) == -1)
            return -1;
        }
        else {
          /* Read and answer each query. */
          while (nr_queries > 0) {
            what = "reading query string length";
            if (opt_index+4 > optlen)
              goto opt_meta_invalid_option_len;
